long_biography.plain_text:
Property entrepreneur Roger Lips entered the industry after studying business economics and working at Hevo and Bouwfonds Woningontwikkeling. His first independent deal involved buying a heavily financed building and reselling it. He then pursued redevelopment opportunities, including converting Berlicum's former town hall into shops and homes. Keeping some properties for rental income while selling development projects helped him expand.

Bank loans also left Lips exposed when the financial crisis brought payment difficulties. His Dutch property business collapsed in 2013, and he subsequently moved to Dubai. In 2024, a Dutch court sentenced him to four years in prison for bankruptcy fraud, finding that he had removed assets from bankruptcy estates to protect his own financial interests. He appealed the conviction.
